argumentsFor: Export Promotion Councils can connect sectoral exporters with government and overseas markets.

example.text: Suppose a sectoral council identifies demand in several new destinations and helps exporters understand differing product standards. Diversification would be meaningful only if firms can meet those standards competitively and deliver reliably.

question.answer: The councils can translate sector-specific exporter concerns into coordinated action on market intelligence, standards, logistics and access. sections.heading: Competitiveness before expansion
paragraphs: The stated policy objective combines stronger competitiveness with wider markets. A firm that cannot meet quality, cost, delivery and regulatory requirements will not gain durable market share merely by entering additional destinations.

sections.heading: Institutional bridge
paragraphs: Export Promotion Councils can serve as sectoral interfaces between exporters and government. Their value lies in converting market information and exporter needs into practical support, while avoiding duplication and tracking results.

advisory_notes: The release text supports additional details such as the Export Promotion Mission, MSMEs, FTAs, DGFT coordination and visits to Germany and the Netherlands; the note appropriately treats these as analysis rather than claiming them as source
The definition of export competitiveness is a useful analytical framing, but it is not a definition supplied by the release and should remain clearly presented as an explanatory formulation.
The claim that diversification reduces dependence and improves resilience is sound policy analysis, but outcomes are conditional on demand, standards, finance and logistics.

The background claim that EPCs connect exporters with government and overseas markets is supported generally by official material, though individual councils differ in legal basis and functions.[1][2]
The use line's reference to global value chains is a reasonable GS3 linkage, but the release does not expressly use that phrase as an outcome or assessment.
The GS2.7 linkage is defensible for pressure groups and institutional interfaces, but EPCs should not be described as ordinary pressure groups without qualification.
The pocketRead headline, deck, paragraphs and applied-question answer are analytical summaries rather than independently established facts; retain that framing.
The hypothetical council example is clearly labelled as an illustration and contains no arithmetic or factual event claim requiring correction.

wayForward: Set sector-specific, measurable export outcomes rather than relying only on consultations.
Strengthen exporter access to standards information, testing, certification, trade finance, logistics and market intelligence.
Prioritise diversification based on demand, comparative capability and regulatory feasibility.
Include MSMEs and emerging exporters through simplified procedures, mentoring and digital access.
